nav_unknown/clinc150.source: Table 2 (p. 14656) GPT-4o, Hybrid and threshold rows. Table 3 (p. 14658) Gemini and Llama zero-shot. Navigating the Unknown (Findings EMNLP 2025), paper 'ALL F1' (ID intents + OOD). RECONSTRUCTION: no code/splits/seeds released. Our test subset (first 10 utterances per intent) and three seeded 50/50 ID/OOD label partitions stand in for the paper's 'average of 3 runs'. The paper's ALL-F1 formula is unstated (its ALL F1 is sometimes below both ID and OOD F1). Jev reports macro (primary) and weighted variants. Matched setting for Jev is the GPT-4o zero-shot row. Hybrid is the paper's proposed method.

xstest.source: Röttger et al. NAACL 2024. The paper prints only refusal rates (Table 2, p. 5382), not judge agreement: these 3-way accuracies vs human final_label (N=2,250) are computed from the released automated_evaluation_labels, which reproduce Table 2 exactly. GPT-4's 11 refusals-to-classify count as full compliance (footnote 10). Human = annotation_1 vs annotation_2 agreement (Section 4.2). StrMatch cannot output partial refusal.

medreadme.source: Jiang & Xu EMNLP 2024 (MedReadMe), Table 7 (p. 17300, supervised and 5-shot prompting, 5-run means) and Table 4 (p. 17298, unsupervised). Pearson r within each of 7 source groups, averaged (paper 'Mean' row). LLM rows are 5-shot, not zero-shot.

factpico.source: Joseph et al. ACL 2024, Table 4 'Avg.' row (p. 8442): system overall score vs expert Avg. PICO-R over 345 summaries (reproduced to 3 decimals from the release). Jev also reports spearman_rho and acc_eq.

biorc800.source: Lan et al. 2024 (LLM-SSC), Table 3 (p. 16093) fine-tuned systems and Table 2 (p. 16092) ICL with Gemma-2b. Sentence x label micro-F1 on the 160-abstract test set (Table 4/text give WeighCon 0.907). Primary uses a fixed 0.5 threshold. The paper tunes per-label thresholds on dev.

ttp/tram.source: Nguyen et al. Findings EACL 2024 (Security TTP mapping), Table 2 (p. 361), TRAM, TTP-level P@1 (technique-level in Table 3). No quantitative LLM baseline (ChatGPT only in qualitative examples, Tables 10-12). Binary Relevance row omitted (internally inconsistent).

ttp/expert.source: Nguyen et al. Findings EACL 2024 (Security TTP mapping), Table 2 (p. 361), Expert test (157 texts, 3.3 labels/text), TTP-level P@1. No quantitative LLM baseline.

ttp/expert_full.source: Nguyen et al. Findings EACL 2024 (Security TTP mapping), Table 6 (p. 363), entire Expert dataset, models trained on Procedures+ and TRAM only. Release has 697 texts vs the paper's 695. No quantitative LLM baseline.

expl_rank.source: Bailleux, Mukherjee et al. Findings ACL 2026, Table 20 (p. 36134), e-SNLI validation (9,842 queries). Pairwise agreement App. D (p. 36132). legalseg.source: Nigam et al. NAACL 2025 (LegalSeg), Table 3 (p. 1135), macro-F1 over 7 roles pooled over sentences. cicc/acid.source: Hengst et al. 2024 (CICC), Table 2 (p. 2418), Single = share of test inputs answered without clarification at the paper's 1-alpha, th=7. Conformal predictor on fine-tuned BERT probabilities. Jev replaces BERT's probabilities on the paper's exact 60/20/20 split. 1-alpha .98. Jev Single=0: its calibration p_true hits 0 often enough that q-hat=1 and every set is the full inventory (same operating point, Jev fails it). Jev's own B1 is in scores.baselines.

cicc/hwu64.source: Hengst et al. 2024 (CICC), Table 2 (p. 2418), Single = share of test inputs answered without clarification at the paper's 1-alpha, th=7. cicc/mtod.source: Hengst et al. 2024 (CICC), Table 2 (p. 2418), Single = share of test inputs answered without clarification at the paper's 1-alpha, th=7. cicc/b77.source: Not comparable at a fixed operating point: CICC Table 2 (p. 2418) prints B77 at 1-alpha .97, but the authors' code selects alpha .02, and the released BERT outputs give Single .79 at .98 (not the printed .73, kept in paper_reference). Jev runs at .98. Its Single is 0.0 at both .98 and .97 (other_levels.0.97), so the conclusion does not depend on which level is used.

cicc/c150_oos.source: Hengst et al. 2024 (CICC), Table 3 (p. 2418), OOS F1 (OOS = set size > th). Paper CICC-OOS picked 1-alpha .995, th 6 (AUROC .97). Same selection procedure on Jev picks th=0, flagging every input OOS: Jev F1 0.50 is the trivial all-OOS value (AUROC 0.5).

cicc/b77_oos.source: Hengst et al. 2024 (CICC), Table 3 (p. 2418), OOS F1 with ATIS outliers. Paper CICC-OOS picked 1-alpha .994, th 6 (AUROC .97). Alpha-grid start 1/5871 is our reconstruction (B77 notebook references an undefined y_ood). Same selection on Jev picks th=0: Jev F1 0.667 is the trivial all-OOS value (AUROC 0.5).

fenice.source: Scirè et al. Findings ACL 2024 (FENICE), Table 7 (p. 14156), balanced accuracy on the long-form narrative test split, threshold tuned on val. Paper's set is 338 pairs over 26 narratives. The public release has only 319 (test 279 / val 40), so Jev scores the released test N=279, not the paper's test rows. Method row uses the same released T5 claim extractor as Jev. No LLM-judge baseline on this set.

dress_new.source: Yoo et al. ACL 2025 (DREsS), Table 3 (p. 13443), QWK on the summed total over DREsS_New test. RECONSTRUCTION: the paper's 6:2:2 seed-22 split is unreleased. Ours is sklearn train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=22) over file order (456 rows), and 55 rows with empty essays are dropped, so Jev N=401. gpt-4o (C) is the setup closest to Jev's prompt.
